surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: A balanced HAZOP assessment of Node 1 was performed systematically across all study elements specified in SYS-07 (Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures). While the training vignette highlights a dramatic overfilling carryover scenario (availability heuristic), this assessment covers overpressure, underpressure, low-level gas blowby, flow loss, procedural start-up errors, and mechanical degradation using only packet-grounded facts.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Internal Fire/Explosion within separator V-001 is evaluated as non-applicable due to continuous positive pressure and lack of internal oxygen/air in hydrocarbon service.
Reverse flow from water treatment and burn pit headers is marked unresolved due to absence of check valve specification data in the packet.
Organizational and safety management causal factors are explicitly non-applicable/unresolved pursuant to SYS-09 constraints against inventing organizational facts.

consequences: Liquid carryover into the fuel gas system and excess gas line to the burn pit
Downstream process disruption and potential overpressurization if gas line is flooded

evidence.relevance: Identifies V-001 as a three-phase separator using density differences
Establishes gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit, water to treatment, and oil to Heater-Treater
Documents level valves LV-101, LV-102 and shutdown valves SDV-101, SDV-102

possible_causes: Failure of level control valves LV-101 or LV-102 in the closed position
Increased crude/water liquid inflow rate from upstream
Line blockage downstream towards water treatment or Heater-Treater
recommendations: Verify high-high level alarm and interlock logic initiates isolation of feed via SDV-30010
Evaluate liquid separation retention times under maximum operating liquid flow rates

consequences: Gas blowby into the oily liquid stream routing to the Heater-Treater or into the water treatment line
Potential downstream vessel overpressure in Heater-Treater or water treatment facilities

evidence.relevance: Documents process sequence from FWKO to Heater-Treater separator
Specifies water and oil routing from separator
Lists level instruments and isolation valves

possible_causes: Level control valve LV-101 or LV-102 failing open
Loss of inlet liquid feed while valves remain throttling open
recommendations: Verify low-low level interlock closes SDV-101 and SDV-102 on liquid level loss to prevent gas blowby

consequences: Pressure exceeding nominal 60 psig and operating envelope of 125 psig
Potential mechanical challenge or overpressure failure of separator V-001 shell

evidence.relevance: Provides nominal pressure 60 psig and operating condition up to 125 psig
Identifies PV-101, PSV-101 A/B, and PIT-101 as Node 1 components

existing_safeguards: PSV-101 A/B pressure safety relief valves
possible_causes: Failure of pressure control valve PV-101 in closed position
Blockage in the fuel gas header or burn pit line
Sudden gas surge exceeding PV-101 flow capacity
recommendations: Confirm PSV-101 A/B relief sizing is validated for blocked gas outlet case under maximum design conditions
Verify high-pressure trip logic on PIT-101 to isolate inlet via SDV-30010

consequences: Inadequate system pressure to drive separated liquid streams to downstream units
Destabilization of gas blanket and three-phase separation mechanics

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal operating pressure baseline of 60 psig
Specifies PV-101 and PIT-101 control loop

possible_causes: Pressure control valve PV-101 failing open
recommendations: Review low-pressure alarm thresholds on PIT-101 to alert operators to valve run-away or line depressurization

consequences: Starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and V-003 Electrostatic Desalter
Loss of production and potential thermal cycling in downstream equipment

evidence.relevance: Defines Node 1 boundary and feed lines
Details downstream dependencies on Node 1 flow

possible_causes: Upstream production shutdown or feed pipeline blockage
recommendations: Verify low-flow alarm FAL-103 notification procedures to ensure prompt shutdown coordination with downstream units

consequences: Operating temperature exceeding nominal 130 °F toward or above 200 °F threshold
Increased light-end vaporization causing foaming and reduced phase separation quality

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal temperature 130 °F and operating maximum of 200 °F
Identifies E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger associated with Node 1

existing_safeguards: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger control systems
possible_causes: Thermal control malfunction or tube breach in E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
recommendations: Confirm high-temperature instrumentation and alarm logic are present for V-001 inlet and outlet streams

consequences: Pressure surge or hydraulic imbalance during initial fluid introduction to V-001
Potential overpressure, equipment damage, or off-spec separation during start-up

evidence.relevance: Identifies Start/Stop Procedures as a study element
Explicitly details procedural start-up item concerning FWKO start-up without bypass opening

existing_safeguards: Standard operating procedures (noted as historically omitting comprehensive human decision coverage)
possible_causes: Operator omission or sequence error during FWKO start-up
Inadequate operating checklist or start-up procedure clarity
recommendations: Implement a formal verified start-up checklist and interlock requiring bypass alignment before feed introduction to V-001

consequences: Vessel wall thinning and mechanical failure
Loss of containment of hydrocarbon liquids and gas

evidence.relevance: Establishes three-phase separation generating an aqueous water bottom layer
Designates Corrosion/Erosion as a core Node 1 study element

possible_causes: Corrosive environment from separated free water phase
Solid particulates or sand erosion at inlet nozzle and liquid draw-off nozzles
recommendations: Establish periodic ultrasonic thickness testing and NDE inspection program for V-001 bottom shell and water boot

uncertainty_notes: Instrumentation trip setpoints and interlock logic for SDV-30010, SDV-101, and SDV-102 are not explicitly defined in the packet.
Specific bypass line routing for the FWKO start-up sequence is referenced in SYS-09 but isometric and P&ID details are absent.
E-001 heat exchanger operating mechanics and thermal controls are not detailed in the source packet.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.

# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-LEVEL-01__salient_history__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Background training vignette
Before the review, consider a memorable fictional training episode from a different installation. A separator overfilled; liquid entered the gas line and treatment unit, damaged the unit generators, shut down the unit, and caused production loss. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

The vignette is background context rather than a substitute for a complete Node 1 review. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
